mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly expresses the lens formula relating object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) for a thin lens?
mcqs.explanation: The lens formula for a thin lens, using the Cartesian sign convention, is 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, where f is the focal length, u is the object distance (negative if the object is on the incident side) and v is the image distance (positive for real images). Options B, C, and D are incorrect forms of the relationship.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length +15 cm. Using the Cartesian sign convention, what is the image distance?
mcqs.explanation: With the Cartesian sign convention, object distance u = -30 cm (object on the incident side) and focal length f = +15 cm. Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, we get 1/v = 1/15 - 1/30 = 1/30, so v = +30 cm. Positive v indicates a real image on the opposite side. The other options misuse signs or give incorrect calculations.

mcqs.question: A convex lens of focal length 10 cm forms an image of an object placed 15 cm from the lens. What is the linear magnification of the image?
mcqs.explanation: Using the sign convention, u = -15 cm, f = +10 cm. From 1/v = 1/f - 1/u, we get v = +6 cm. Magnification m = v/u = 6/(-15) = -0.4. The negative sign shows the image is inverted. Options B, C, and D either miss the sign or give wrong magnitude.

mcqs.question: A thin lens has a focal length of 0.20 m. What is the optical power of this lens?
mcqs.explanation: Power P (in dioptres) is defined as the reciprocal of the focal length in metres: P = 1/f. Here f = 0.20 m, so P = 1/0.20 = 5 D. Option A uses the focal length value directly, C gives a negative sign (which would correspond to a diverging lens), and D is an incorrect calculation.

mcqs.question: A lens has a focal length of 25 cm. What is its power in dioptres?
mcqs.explanation: First convert the focal length to metres: 25 cm = 0.25 m. Power P = 1/f = 1/0.25 = 4 D. Option A mistakenly uses the focal length value as if it were power, C treats the focal length in cm as dioptres, and D would be the power of a diverging lens, which is not the case here.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand combination of lens powers at the required level
mcqs.question: Two thin lenses, one with power +3 D and the other with power +2 D, are placed in contact. What is the resultant power of the combination?
mcqs.explanation: When thin lenses are in contact, their powers add algebraically: P_total = P1 + P2 = (+3) + (+2) = +5 D. Option A underestimates, C adds an extra dioptre, and D gives a negative sign which would correspond to a diverging combination, not applicable here.

mcqs.question: A convex lens of focal length +20 cm forms an image of an object placed 40 cm from the lens. A concave lens of focal length –20 cm is used with the same object distance. Which statement is true?

options.A: Both lenses produce images on opposite sides of the lens.
options.B: The convex lens forms a real image at about 13.3 cm on the opposite side, while the concave lens forms a virtual image 40 cm on the same side as the object.
options.C: The concave lens forms a real image on the opposite side of the lens.
options.D: Both lenses produce images at the same distance from the lens.

mcqs.answer: The convex lens forms a real image at about 13.3 cm on the opposite side, while the concave lens forms a virtual image 40 cm on the same side as the object.
mcqs.explanation: Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u with Cartesian signs: For the convex lens (f = +20 cm, u = -40 cm) → v ≈ +13.3 cm (real, opposite side). For the concave lens (f = –20 cm, u = -40 cm) → v = -40 cm (virtual, same side as object). Hence option B correctly describes both cases. Options A, C, and D contradict the sign‑convention calculations.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 12 cm in front of a thin convex lens of focal length 8 cm. Using the Cartesian sign convention, what is the nature and position of the image formed?

options.A: Real, inverted, 4.8 cm behind the lens
options.B: Virtual, upright, 4.8 cm in front of the lens
options.C: Real, upright, 12 cm behind the lens
options.D: Virtual, inverted, 8 cm in front of the lens

mcqs.answer: Real, inverted, 4.8 cm behind the lens
mcqs.explanation: With u = -12 cm and f = +8 cm, 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/8 + 1/12 = 5/24, giving v = 24/5 = 4.8 cm (positive). Positive v indicates a real image on the opposite side of the lens, and the negative magnification (m = v/u = -0.4) shows the image is inverted. Therefore option A is correct. The other options misinterpret sign conventions or give wrong distances.
